jailor.action: Choose a prisoner during the day; question them privately that night. From N2, you can execute instead of releasing them.
jailor.keyRule: Three executions total. Executing Town removes your jail ability. Choose a different prisoner on consecutive nights.
jailor.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
jailor.example: D2 select 7; N2 hear their claim, then release or attempt an execution. Selecting Execute does not guarantee a death.

marshal.action: Start a daytime Tribunal to execute nominated players without the usual defense and judgment.
marshal.keyRule: Two Tribunal uses, normally up to two executions per Tribunal. Roles and wills stay hidden until the Tribunal ends. No night ability.
marshal.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
marshal.example: If you execute 4, you must decide whether to execute 9 before seeing 4’s role. Have evidence for both first.

mayor.action: Reveal during the day to increase the weight of your vote. You have no night action.
mayor.keyRule: Reveal adds one vote immediately; each later day adds another. You cannot Reveal on D1 or while on trial.
mayor.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
mayor.example: If your extra vote changes today’s majority, Reveal before you are put on trial.

monarch.action: Knight a player at night to give them a lasting extra vote. You have two Knight charges.
monarch.keyRule: You gain Basic Defense while a Knight is alive. Knighthood grants voting power, not proof that its recipient is Town.
monarch.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
monarch.example: Knight 4; check that the effect completed. If no Knight remains alive, do not assume you still have its defense.

prosecutor.action: Prosecute during the day to force your chosen player’s execution without normal judgment.
prosecutor.keyRule: Two charges, at most one use per day from D2. Prosecuting Town removes the remaining charges. No night ability.
prosecutor.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
prosecutor.example: A supported case against 9 can justify Prosecute; using it merely to prove your role can cost Town an ally.

coroner.action: Autopsy a dead player during the day to collect their killer’s role. At night, Examine a living suspect against the killer records you have collected.
coroner.keyRule: You need an Autopsy before a useful Examine. Records accumulate; no match means no match to your records, not confirmed Town.
coroner.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
coroner.example: Autopsy dead 6, then Examine 9. Report the corpse, killer role and match result separately.

investigator.action: Investigate a player for Murder, Trespassing, both crimes, or No Crime.
investigator.keyRule: Murder concerns an attack that night. Trespassing concerns an opposing-faction visit at some point in the game. Neither result alone reveals allegiance.
investigator.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
investigator.example: A Town player can have Trespassing; No Crime does not mean the checked player is harmless.

lookout.action: Watch a player’s house and learn the identities of its visible visitors.
lookout.keyRule: You see who came to the watched house, not where its owner went or the visitors’ roles. Astral visits are invisible.
lookout.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
lookout.example: Watch 4; see 7 and 9 visiting 4. That says nothing about whom 4 visited.

psychic.action: Choose a player to include in a vision. Odd nights give two names with at least one appearing Good; even nights give three with at least one appearing Evil.
psychic.keyRule: The group includes your chosen target. It does not identify which member fits, and it does not mean exactly one.
psychic.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
psychic.example: N1 Good: 4 and 9 means at least one appears Good. N2 Evil: 2, 7 and 11 means at least one appears Evil.

seer.action: Compare two players and learn whether their apparent factions are Friends or Enemies.
seer.keyRule: You visit both players. You cannot use yourself, revealed Town members or any player you have already selected earlier in the game.
seer.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
seer.example: 4 and 9 are Enemies: their apparent factions differ. It does not say which player opposes Town.

sheriff.action: Search one player at night for Innocent or Suspicious feedback.
sheriff.keyRule: This checks apparent suspicion, not exact role or guaranteed allegiance. Some enemies appear Innocent, and framing can make allies Suspicious.
sheriff.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
sheriff.example: A roleblocked Search is no result. Do not enter Innocent merely because no suspicion message appeared.

spy.action: Place a permanent Bug on a house to learn about evil-role visitors. Old Bugs can report on later nights.
spy.keyRule: Record the bugged house and reported role separately. A quiet Bug is not a Town clear, and a role report does not give the visitor’s player number.
spy.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
spy.example: Bug 4 on N1; on N3 it reports a Jinx visit to 4 even though you placed tonight’s new Bug elsewhere.

tracker.action: Follow a player and learn their visible destinations, or that they made no visible visit.
tracker.keyRule: This shows outgoing movement. Astral actions are invisible, so no visible visit does not prove that the player used no ability.
tracker.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
tracker.example: Track 4 and see 9: player 4 went to 9. It does not mean player 9 visited 4.

bodyguard.action: Guard a player to intercept one direct harmful visitor, stop that harmful action and fight the visitor.
bodyguard.keyRule: The fight deals Powerful attacks to the attacker and to you. Self Protect is different: two uses of Basic Defense at home. Grace Period disables N1 protection.
bodyguard.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
bodyguard.example: Guard 4 and intercept an attacker: 4 avoids that action, but you can die in the fight. A quiet Guard is not a save.

cleric.action: Barrier one player for Powerful Defense that night, stopping Basic and Powerful attacks.
cleric.keyRule: Your named-target attack notice means the target was attacked. Quiet nights give no save notice. Self Barrier has one use; Grace Period disables N1 protection.
cleric.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
cleric.example: Barrier 4; if 4 is attacked, you can receive attack feedback while 4 receives the separate Barrier notice. Unstoppable attacks still bypass this defense.

crusader.action: Fortify one player with Powerful Defense and attack one random direct visitor to their house.
crusader.keyRule: Your visitor attack can hit Town. Target-attack feedback and visitor-attack feedback are separate; neither identifies the struck visitor. Grace Period disables N1 protection.
crusader.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
crusader.example: Fortify 4; a friendly Sheriff visiting 4 can be hit. You do not automatically learn that visitor’s identity.

oracle.action: Choose a Town role, not a player number, and protect its holders with Powerful Defense for that night.
oracle.keyRule: Aegis is astral: it makes no ordinary visible visit. Do not choose the same role consecutively; Oracle itself is once-only. Grace Period disables N1 Aegis.
oracle.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
oracle.example: Aegis Sheriff covers actual Sheriffs, not everyone claiming Sheriff. Its protection notice names neither a player nor a role.

trapper.action: Build a Trap for one night, then place it at a player’s house. It stays there until triggered or dismantled.
trapper.keyRule: Only one active Trap. A harmful trigger attacks and intercepts the visitor; a non-harmful trigger reveals visitor roles. Rebuild before placing again after a trigger.
trapper.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
trapper.example: N1 Build; N2 place on 4; N3 trigger; N4 rebuild; N5 place again. A quiet existing Trap is not a new nightly visit.

deputy.action: Use your single daytime High Noon shot on a supported suspect. You have no night ability.
deputy.keyRule: Available from D2. A miss can result from apparent Town status or defense and still spends your only shot; it is private feedback.
deputy.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
deputy.example: D3 shoot 9 and miss: record the miss and stop claiming further shots. A held shot is not a miss.

trickster.action: Place a Magic Mirror to absorb a qualifying direct attack. After absorbing one, use Unleash to send that stored attack at another player.
trickster.keyRule: You cannot place another Mirror while storing an attack. Self Mirror is once-only; an Unstoppable attack shatters a Mirror. No absorption means no stored shot.
trickster.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
trickster.example: N2 Mirror 4 absorbs a Vigilante attack; N3 Unleash it on a supported target, or hold it without placing another Mirror.

veteran.action: Choose Alert to defend yourself and shoot your direct visitors that night; choose No Alert to save a charge.
veteran.keyRule: Three Alerts. Alert gives Basic Defense and Powerful attacks, including against Town visitors. Shot feedback is a count, not visitor identities.
veteran.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
veteran.example: Alert and shoot two visitors: that does not prove both died or tell you which players they were.

vigilante.action: Load a bullet on a night you do not shoot, then Shoot a player on a later night.
vigilante.keyRule: Three bullets to load; Load and Shoot take separate nights. Shooting Town removes your gun. A surviving target is not automatically evil.
vigilante.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
vigilante.example: N1 Load, N2 Shoot, N3 Load. If a Town-hit penalty removes the gun, you cannot keep loading or firing.

admirer.action: Use your starting subalignment clue to find your Obsession with Admire. Finding them unlocks Care, protecting both of you.
admirer.keyRule: Care has two uses. Daytime Bestow has two separate uses and grants lasting astral visits plus roleblock/control immunity. Care is unavailable before discovery.
admirer.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
admirer.example: Admire 4 and find your Obsession; a later Care protects both of you. Bestow is a separate day action, not another Admire.

amnesiac.action: Automatically Remember an eligible dead Town role in the morning, then play as that role.
amnesiac.keyRule: You do not select a corpse by visiting it at night. Town Power gets priority; once you remember, use the new role’s actions and limits.
amnesiac.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
amnesiac.example: N1 wait; D2 remember Sheriff; from N2, use Search rather than inventing an Amnesiac night action.

retributionist.action: Raise an eligible dead Town player, then choose where their borrowed ability acts. You receive that ability’s feedback.
retributionist.keyRule: You visit the corpse; the zombie visits its destination. You need a usable body, cannot normally use Stoned corpses or protect yourself, and are roleblock/control immune.
retributionist.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
retributionist.example: Raise dead Sheriff 6 to check living 9. Report both numbers and the borrowed result; an unavailable corpse gives no check.

socialite.action: Add guests during the day, then Party at a house to reject uninvited visitors.
socialite.keyRule: Two manual guests total, at most one added per day. Do not Party at the same house consecutively. This obstructs incoming visits, not the resident’s outgoing ability.
socialite.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
socialite.example: Party at 4 can stop an uninvited player reaching 4. A rejection notice does not name that visitor.

tavern-keeper.action: Drink with a player to attempt to roleblock their night action.
tavern-keeper.keyRule: After a successful block, Hangover prevents an immediate repeat block or Control. You are roleblock immune; visiting certain killers can make them retaliate.
tavern-keeper.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
tavern-keeper.example: Drink with 4 on N1; choose someone else on N2. No deaths after the block does not prove 4 is the killer.

catalyst.action: Overcharge a player so their ability can act twice on its following day or night cycle.
catalyst.keyRule: The recipient’s role determines the timing and effect. Applying Overcharge is not itself proof that two actions succeeded.
catalyst.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
catalyst.example: Overcharge a night actor on N1; confirm their following cycle rather than promising two actions on the application night.

pilgrim.action: You have no active ability. Help Town by comparing claims, asking useful questions and voting.
pilgrim.keyRule: No night targets or special results. Public observations belong in day notes, and Pilgrim must be permitted by the setup.
pilgrim.win: Help Town eliminate its enemies, including Coven and hostile killing factions. You share Town’s victory even if dead; your ability has no separate win quota.
pilgrim.example: “7 changed their N1 target” records a public contradiction; it is not a private investigative result.

archmage.action: Retrain a teammate into an available Common Coven role, or retrain yourself into an available Coven Killing or Coven Power role.
archmage.keyRule: A role change needs legal availability and the actual resulting role. Book attacks are an alternative to Retrain, not a simultaneous extra action.
archmage.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
archmage.example: Retrain an ally only when the replacement solves a team problem; verify the changed role before planning its next ability.

hex-master.action: Hex one player each night. Marks persist, so spread them among opponents likely to stay alive.
hex-master.keyRule: Hex Bomb automatically kills the Hexed opponents once every living non-Coven player is Hexed and you are alive at resolution, usually dawn. No Bomb button or Necronomicon is required.
hex-master.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
hex-master.example: Only 4, 7 and 9 remain outside Coven; 4 and 7 are Hexed. Hex 9, or have 9 eliminated, to complete the Bomb condition. Stay alive through resolution.

witch.action: Control one player into a second destination. Your faction learns the controlled player’s role; you receive their borrowed ability feedback.
witch.keyRule: You normally visit only the first player. Change that player on consecutive nights. Revealing them Illuminates them, making them unavailable to Blood Ritual.
witch.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
witch.example: Control Sheriff 4 into 9: your visible destination is 4; the borrowed Search checks 9. No completed Control means no borrowed result.

conjurer.action: Use your one daytime Meteor from D2 for a Powerful attack. With the book, you can also make normal night attacks.
conjurer.keyRule: Meteor does not publicly name you as its caster, but its attack is public. A defended Meteor still spends the single use.
conjurer.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
conjurer.example: Save Meteor for a consequential removal; a failed kill does not restore the charge.

ritualist.action: Blood Ritual guesses an eligible player’s exact role for an astral Unstoppable attack.
ritualist.keyRule: Two attempts. A wrong guess spends one and can give no failure notice. You cannot guess Town Investigatives or Illuminated players; Grace Period blocks N1 Ritual.
ritualist.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
ritualist.example: A confident exact-role guess can kill through ordinary protection, but not Invincible Defense. Guessing a broad alignment is not an exact-role Ritual.

jinx.action: Choose a house and attack one random non-Coven visitor. With the book, you also attack its resident.
jinx.keyRule: Other direct visitors can learn your identity and the house, including a surviving victim. An attack notice gives no full visitor list.
jinx.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
jinx.example: Jinx 4; if several players visit, an unhit witness can identify you. A quiet house gives no visitor attack.

dreamweaver.action: Dreamweave a Town player. If no Town visit cures them the following night, they develop Insomnia and lose day and night ability use.
dreamweaver.keyRule: Dreamweave is delayed, not an instant roleblock. Your death or retraining normally clears the effect.
dreamweaver.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
dreamweaver.example: Weave 4 on N1; a Town visitor on N2 can cure them. Without that cure, Insomnia develops afterward.

enchanter.action: Enchant to falsify investigative appearances. Or spend one of two Alterates to forge a player’s shown death role, faction and will.
enchanter.keyRule: Enchant does not reveal the target’s true role. An Alterate must coincide with the target’s death that night; a surviving target does not show the forgery.
enchanter.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
enchanter.example: Coordinate Alterate 4 with a planned death. Do not call a living player successfully forged just because you selected a replacement will.

illusionist.action: Illusion an ally to disguise their investigative appearance. Use one Phantasm for the living team, or set your own displayed death role and faction.
illusionist.keyRule: These effects change appearances, not real roles or loyalties. A book attack replaces the ordinary protection choice; Illusion does not stop Bodyguard/Trap interception.
illusionist.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
illusionist.example: Illusion the acting book holder to hide investigative evidence; do not promise that this shields them from every defensive role.

medusa.action: Spend up to three Stone Gazes to permanently mark players. If a marked player dies, opponents cannot read their role or will.
medusa.keyRule: Stone is not a kill or protection. You start self-Stoned; marked deaths remain readable to Coven. A visible N1 Stone can contradict an unavailable TP cover.
medusa.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
medusa.example: Stone 4 tonight; if 4 dies on a later night, their hidden role/will effect still applies. Holding Stone creates no ordinary Stone visit.

necromancer.action: Reanimate an eligible corpse and direct its borrowed ability to a destination. You receive its feedback.
necromancer.keyRule: You visit the corpse, not its destination. Each usable evil corpse is once-only; Town corpses can be reused. Book attacks replace ordinary reanimation.
necromancer.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
necromancer.example: Use dead Sheriff 6 to check 9. A missing or unsuitable corpse is a failure, not an Innocent result.

poisoner.action: Choose Drink to roleblock a player, or Smog to obstruct visits into their house.
poisoner.keyRule: Drink affects the resident’s action; Smog affects incoming visitors. Smog cannot accompany a book attack and can obstruct Coven teammates.
poisoner.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
poisoner.example: Smog 4 can stop your own teammate reaching 4. Drink 4 instead tries to stop 4 from acting.

potion-master.action: Choose Barrier for Powerful Defense or Reveal to learn a player’s role with Coven. The book adds a Harmful attack potion.
potion-master.keyRule: Use one mode for the night. Reveal also Illuminates the player, blocking Blood Ritual on them. Quiet Barrier feedback is not a save.
potion-master.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
potion-master.example: Reveal 4 supplies role knowledge; Barrier 4 supplies protection. The same visit cannot be reported as both modes without a real extra-action effect.

voodoo-master.action: Choose a doll: Silence stops next-day speech, Deafen hides next-day chat, or Blind hides night feedback.
voodoo-master.keyRule: Do not target the same player on consecutive nights, even with a different doll. With the book, the selected effect can also carry an attack.
voodoo-master.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
voodoo-master.example: Blind an information role to suppress its result; do not describe that effect as an ordinary roleblock or assume no victim report means failure.

wildling.action: Sense a player’s visible destinations and visitors. In text mode, you also overhear whispers.
wildling.keyRule: Outgoing destinations and incoming visitors are separate lists. Astral travel is invisible; whisper content is separate from Sense feedback.
wildling.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
wildling.example: Sense 4: “went to 9; visitors 7 and 11” means three different relationships, not a list of everyone you personally visited.

covenite.action: You have no special role ability. Coordinate with Coven; if you hold the book, use its night attack.
covenite.keyRule: No book means no Covenite night action. The role must be permitted by the setup; team information is not your own investigation.
covenite.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
covenite.example: An N1 hold without the book is normal. Do not invent a target or result merely to fill your private history.

cultist.action: Use your one daytime Indoctrinate to convert an eligible Town player into Coven, retaining their role and abilities.
cultist.keyRule: Successful recruitment ends your Basic Defense. Confirm the faction change; a book attack is separate from the daytime conversion.
cultist.win: Help Coven eliminate Town and other opposing factions. You share Coven’s victory even if dead; your special effect is a tool, not a separate win quota.
cultist.example: Convert a Cleric: they remain Cleric but now win with Coven. You have not changed their role into Cultist.

baker.action: Feed Bread to other players at night. Get three other living players with Bread to become Famine.
baker.keyRule: Your own starting Bread is not one of those three recipients. If fewer than three others remain, all living players must have Bread instead.
baker.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Transforming unlocks your stronger form; transformation alone is not a win.
baker.example: Feed 4, 7 and 9 and keep them alive. A fed player dying before completion removes them from the living-recipient count.

berserker.action: You start attacking on N2. Actual kills build your strength toward War.
berserker.keyRule: First kill: Powerful attack. Second: Rampage. Third: transform into War, gaining two-target Unstoppable Rampages and Invincible Defense. A survived attempt adds no kill.
berserker.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Transforming unlocks your stronger form; transformation alone is not a win.
berserker.example: N2 attack and kill gives progress; N3 attack stopped by defense does not. Count kills, not the nights you pressed Attack.

plaguebearer.action: Infect players until every other living player is infected. Contact with infected players spreads the infection; your two starting neighbors begin infected.
plaguebearer.keyRule: Completing infection transforms you into Pestilence. Passive spread counts too; already infected players are not new progress.
plaguebearer.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Transforming unlocks your stronger form; transformation alone is not a win.
plaguebearer.example: Infect an active visitor so their contacts spread infection. Watch the living infection markers, not just your direct target list.

soul-collector.action: Reap players to mark them for extra souls when they die. You also gain one passive soul each night.
soul-collector.keyRule: At seven actual souls you transform into Death. Reap does not kill its target; their later death supplies progress.
soul-collector.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Transforming unlocks your stronger form; transformation alone is not a win.
soul-collector.example: Mark a likely victim, then check the soul counter. Once Death arrives, stop using the old Reap plan.

doomsayer.action: From N2, confirm three simultaneous player/role guesses. All three must be correct in the same set.
doomsayer.keyRule: One wrong guess fails the whole set without identifying the mistake. Do not guess Town Investigative roles; Doom victims die later, not immediately on confirmation.
doomsayer.win: Win by correctly Dooming all three players in one set; you then leave Town in victory. You do not need to eliminate the rest of the town.
doomsayer.example: 4 Cleric, 7 Coven Utility and 9 Vigilante must all match in one submitted set. Two correct guesses are no win.

executioner.action: Read your assigned Town target and get that specific player hanged while you are alive.
executioner.keyRule: Other deaths are not your hanging objective; losing the target that way can turn you into Jester, with a different win requirement.
executioner.win: Win when your assigned target is hanged while you are alive. Hanging someone else or killing the target at night does not satisfy it.
executioner.example: If the assigned target dies to a night attack, do not claim the Executioner win. Follow your new role if you become Jester.

jester.action: Meet the day’s Chatterbox message quota, then get yourself hanged by the trial system.
jester.keyRule: Failing the quota prevents your win even if hanged and can kill you of boredom. A qualifying hanging unlocks a Haunt against an eligible guilty/abstaining voter.
jester.win: Win by being hanged after meeting that day’s Chatterbox quota. Dying to an attack or being hanged with an unmet quota is not enough.
jester.example: Complete the quota before judgment and last words, which do not count. A night death is not the hanging you need.

pirate.action: Scour to find your three secretly assigned Landlubbers. From N2, Plunder can attack one, with three Plunder uses.
pirate.keyRule: All three assigned players must die; other killers can do it. Killing a non-Landlubber with Plunder removes your remaining Plunders. There are no duels.
pirate.win: Stay alive until all three assigned Landlubbers are dead, then leave in victory. Three arbitrary kills do not satisfy the objective.
pirate.example: Scour 4 and find a Landlubber. If someone else kills 4, that still advances your objective while you stay alive.

arsonist.action: Douse players directly and passively Douse your normal visitors. Choose Ignite to burn all previously Doused players.
arsonist.keyRule: Ignite is a separate astral Unstoppable attack. Taking no action can Clean gasoline from yourself; Douse and Clean do not burn targets.
arsonist.win: Win with the Arsonist faction by eliminating its opponents. You do not need to Douse every survivor before choosing Ignite.
arsonist.example: Douse 4 and 7, then choose Ignite on a later night. Do not wait for automatic ignition or mistake a passive visitor for your own visit.

serial-killer.action: Attack at night. Two consecutive kills prepare a Powerful Rampage for your next attack.
serial-killer.keyRule: A night without a kill resets Bloodlust. Cautious prevents your automatic retaliation against roleblockers; it does not cancel your chosen attack.
serial-killer.win: Win with the Serial Killer faction by eliminating its opponents. Bloodlust is a combat upgrade, not a separate victory condition.
serial-killer.example: Kill on two consecutive nights, then plan the stronger attack’s visitor risk. Two attempted attacks that fail do not build the same progress.

shroud.action: Choose a direct attack, or Shroud a player so their direct visits carry Basic attacks.
shroud.keyRule: If the Shrouded player makes no direct visit, the fallback attacks that player instead. Their chosen route determines the victims.
shroud.win: Win with the Shroud faction by eliminating its opponents. A successful Shroud or fallback kill is progress, not an automatic win.
shroud.example: Shroud 4 and they visit 9: the attack follows to 9. If 4 stays home, the fallback attacks 4.

werewolf.action: On human nights, learn a player’s scent and keep receiving their destinations. On Full Moons, Rampage at a house or at home.
werewolf.keyRule: Baseline Full Moons are N2, N4 and every night afterward. Home Rampage attacks your visitors; an existing scent can still report without a new visit.
werewolf.win: Win with the Werewolf faction by eliminating its opponents. Learning every scent is not required.
werewolf.example: Scent 4 on N1; Rampage at 9 on N2 while the old scent can still report where 4 went.

cursed-soul.action: Soul Swap exchanges roles with a player; it does not exchange factions. After swapping, use the new role’s abilities.
cursed-soul.keyRule: In the default Wandering Souls faction, the goal is to remove every remaining Cursed Soul role. Check the actual role gained; the swap can be redirected or randomized.
cursed-soul.win: In the default Wandering Souls faction, eliminate every Cursed Soul role while a Wandering Souls member survives. Your current role and your faction are separate.
cursed-soul.example: Swap into Sheriff and you still belong to Wandering Souls. The player given Cursed Soul keeps their old faction.

vampire.action: Convert an undefended Town player into your Vampire faction, or Drain for a Basic attack. Conversion keeps their existing role.
vampire.keyRule: Three Convert charges. An ineligible Convert falls back to Drain. If you die, a surviving converted faction member can inherit the Vampire role and remaining charges.
vampire.win: Win with the Vampire faction by eliminating or converting its opponents. A single conversion is recruitment, not the win itself.
vampire.example: Convert a Cleric: they keep Barrier but now win with Vampires. Their survival alone does not prove recruitment.

famine.action: You are already Famine. Starve a living Bread recipient to remove one day of Bread and accelerate their starvation.
famine.keyRule: While you remain alive, opponents consume Bread each morning and die when they have none to eat. Do not resume Baker’s Feed plan.
famine.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Keep Famine alive to continue starvation; becoming Famine is not itself a win.
famine.example: A Bread recipient can survive today while their supply shrinks. Keep Famine alive and track the remaining Bread; a Starve selection is not an immediate kill.

war.action: You are already War. Choose up to two distinct houses for Unstoppable Rampages that also attack their visitors.
war.keyRule: Your Invincible Defense stops ordinary attacks, not hanging or defense-ignoring effects. You no longer need Berserker’s three-kill buildup.
war.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Use your Rampages to finish remaining enemies; becoming War is not itself a win.
war.example: Attack 4 and 9 in one night if both destinations are useful; count visitors and team traffic before committing.

pestilence.action: You are already Pestilence. Visit to apply the maximum Pestilence stacks; contacts also spread stacks between players.
pestilence.keyRule: Three stacks kill a player. These stacks replace the earlier infection goal; you are roleblock/obstacle immune, but hanging can still remove you.
pestilence.win: Win with Apocalypse by eliminating its opponents. Stack deaths help remove them; becoming Pestilence is not itself a win.
pestilence.example: A player at one or two stacks can survive. Your selected Spread fills their stacks; track the actual resulting deaths.

death.action: You are already Death. Survive the day of your public transformation until sundown.
death.keyRule: There is no further ordinary Reap action. Surviving the daytime deadline brings Apocalypse against non-Apocalypse players; being hanged first stops that route.
death.win: Survive your transformation day to sundown so Apocalypse resolves for your faction. Transformation alone does not win; daytime execution can still stop you.
death.example: Transform on D5: your decisive task is surviving D5’s votes. You do not need to select another night target.
